newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q3 GDP rises 0.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q3 GDP rises 0.8 percent.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, at 1986 prices, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent in the third quarter from the second quarter, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
The economy grew by 3.3 percent at an annualized rate in the third quarter quarter, the agency said.

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.7 percent rise in the third quarter after the 0.3 percent rise in the second quarter.
Statistics Canada said it was the largest quarterly gain since the the fourth quarter of 1994 and was fueled by merchandise exports, residential construction and a farm inventory build-up.

Statistics Canada said year-over-year growth averaged only 1.1 percent in the first three quarters of 1996. An official added that the fourth quarter would also be hurt by the General Motors strike in October.
During the third quarter, the federal agency said, business investment in machinery and equipment rose 7.4 percent following a drop in the second quarter.

Investment in non-residential construction grew 0.8 percent but remained 10 percent below its peak in the fourth quarter of 1994. Residential construction rose four percent after a six percent gain in the second quarter.

The quarter saw a liquidation in non-farm inventories of C$900 million at 1986 prices, following a C$5.5 billion liquidation in the second. Manufacturers and retailers cut inventories but wholesale trade, utilities and mining added.
Farmers added another C$2.1 billion to inventory, largely as a result of a record grain crop.
Merchandise imports jumped 4.6 percent and exports 2.3 percent. The surplus in 1986 prices fell to C$11.8 billion from an 11-year high of C$16.7 billion in the second.
